Finding: PM2.5 is far higher and more variable at treated than at control stations
Evidence (computed): Mean 80 vs 48 ug/m3; 47% vs 29% of station-days above 60
Consequence for H1: The outcome is skewed: model log(PM2.5) so effects are proportional
Consequence for H2: Levels differ between groups: compare changes, not levels

Evidence (computed): Treated monthly mean: 222 ug/m3 in 2025-11, 30 in 2025-07
Consequence for H1: Season confounds fire and PM2.5: use the winter sample and control for weather
Consequence for H2: A before-and-after comparison is confounded by season: use a weather-based counterfactual

Finding: Strict GRAP stages are rare and confined to a few months
Evidence (computed): Stage 0 in 57% of hours; Stage III/IV 971 hours (6.9%), only between 2025-11 and 2026-01
Consequence for H1: Stage responds to pollution, so it is left out of the primary H1 model
Consequence for H2: H2 rests on a handful of episodes: report each event, not only a pooled number

Finding: The January 2026 outage overlaps the strongest stages
Evidence (computed): 112 of 971 Stage III/IV hours (11.5%) fall in an outage; the longest run is 242 hours from 10 Jan 2026
Consequence for H1: Outage days drop out of the sample
Consequence for H2: Events near the outage must be shown with and without it

Finding: The upwind fire count is small on most days
Evidence (computed): Median 2, SD 5.0, zero on 28% of winter station-days; +10 is about 2.0 SD and occurs on 11% of days
Consequence for H1: Report the effect per +5 detections (about 1 SD) as the primary unit
Consequence for H2: Fire enters the counterfactual only as a control

Finding: Fire counts within 100 km peak in April and May, not in the autumn
Evidence (computed): Mean per day: 12.0 in Oct to Nov 2025, 13.6 in Dec to Feb, 33.3 in April to May
Consequence for H1: The 100 km radius may miss the autumn smoke source: add 200 km and FRP sensitivity runs and say the result is about nearby fires
Consequence for H2: No consequence beyond the fire control

Finding: Weather explains much of PM2.5; some predictors overlap
Evidence (computed): r with PM2.5: boundary layer -0.48, temperature -0.35, pressure +0.33, upwind fire +0.30; strongest predictor pair temperature and pressure (r = -0.83)
Consequence for H1: Control for weather; report variance inflation factors; do not interpret control coefficients on their own
Consequence for H2: A weather-based counterfactual is feasible but must be checked on held-out days

Finding: Treated and control cities move together but differ in level
Evidence (computed): Correlation of daily means 0.71 on 541 days; largest gap in 2025-11 (+149 ug/m3)
Consequence for H1: Control cities give a comparison sample and a place for placebo checks
Consequence for H2: Treated minus control is a useful sensitivity run, but the controls are not a clean counterfactual

Finding: Missing days are linked to outages
Evidence (computed): 84% of station-days are valid; 61% of dropped days contain an outage hour against 23% of kept days
Consequence for H1: Primary: drop outage hours; sensitivity: 12 and 20 hour rules and short-gap interpolation
Consequence for H2: Same, plus the with/without-outage event check
